title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 12

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the programme review take place?
tasks.audioText: The CNC theory tutor will review a sample programme on Monday at one. Students should bring the printed programme extract and the controller glossary. The class will identify programme blocks, axis words and feed information. The tutor will explain why a code should be interpreted in the context of the controller and the complete programme.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which glossary should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The CNC theory tutor will review a sample programme on Monday at one. Students should bring the printed programme extract and the controller glossary. The class will identify programme blocks, axis words and feed information. The tutor will explain why a code should be interpreted in the context of the controller and the complete programme.

tasks.prompt: A CNC programme may contain words that identify axes, positions, feed information and machine functions. The meaning of a code can depend on the controller and the modal state established by earlier blocks. For this reason, a single line should not always be interpreted in isolation. Students should use the approved controller reference and consider the surrounding programme context. Reading 1. Why should a programme line not always be interpreted in isolation?
options: Because its meaning may depend on earlier blocks and the controller state

tasks.prompt: The command ___ in the context of the complete programme.
Choose TWO items that may affect the interpretation of a CNC programme block.
options: The colour of the machine enclosure

tasks.prompt: A command whose effect can remain active in later programme blocks is described as ___.
A code is unfamiliar in a programme extract. What should you do?
options: Guess its meaning from the letter.
Check the approved reference for the specific controller and read the surrounding blocks.
Replace it with a familiar code.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of CNC programme interpretation in a logical order.
options: Check earlier commands and modal information
Identify the controller and programme context
Confirm the meaning in the controller reference
correctOrder: Identify the controller and programme context
Check earlier commands and modal information
Confirm the meaning in the controller reference

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining why CNC programme blocks should be interpreted in context and with reference to the correct controller documentation.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
